prose: Massive amorphous silica supersaturation in the flashing geothermal brine deposited a vitreous glass-like crust inside the 8-inch wellhead choke valve. Steam delivery to Turbine 1 fell 40% before acid descaling could be mobilized.

A seismic shift doubled non-condensible gas fractions (H2S and CO2) in the raw steam to 4.8% by weight. The gas overloaded steam jet ejectors on the main condenser, causing condenser back-pressure to climb and crippling turbine output.

Opening the main steam isolation valve too rapidly heated the 800-meter production casing in under two hours. Unconstrained thermal expansion sheared the anchor flange bolts at the cellar floor, lifting the entire 12-ton wellhead tree four inches.

Reservoir dryout in the eastern fault zone produced 240°C superheated steam with enthalpy surging to 2,980 kJ/kg. The extreme heat scorched high-pressure Teflon valve stem packings and dry-cycled the cyclone moisture separator.

Flashing of dissolved calcium bicarbonate into carbon dioxide at a depth of 550 meters precipitated heavy calcite scale. The crystalline calcium carbonate plugged casing perforations, choking well productivity down to a negligible trickle.

Trace hydrogen chloride vapor carried in high-enthalpy steam formed dilute hydrochloric acid condensate on cold valve bonnet walls. Pitting corrosion perforated the 316-stainless master gate valve, requiring an emergency freeze-plug operation.

Allowing spent geothermal effluent to cool below 80°C prior to reinjection triggered rapid polymerization of monomeric silica. A dense white colloidal silica gelatin formed in the wellbore, completely blocking return permeability into the basement rock.

Emergency bypass venting of 50 tons/hour raw steam through the rock-filled expansion silencer generated 134 dB low-frequency vibration. The intense acoustic standing wave cracked reinforced concrete baffle walls, showering gravel down the exhaust throat.
